explanations.answer: Anyone whose heart moves him to give
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. God tells Moses, "You are to receive My offering from every man whose heart compels him." (Exodus 25:2) So nobody gets drafted. The gift comes from a heart that wants to give, and I think that's the best kind of gift.

explanations.answer: Each man who is twenty or older
explanations.explanation: I see where that came from, friend, but age never comes up here. God says Moses is to receive the offering "from every man whose heart compels him." (Exodus 25:2) The question is about the heart, not a birthday. Nobody has to check an ID at the door.

explanations.answer: The leaders of the twelve tribes
explanations.explanation: Good guess, baker, but the text doesn't name any leaders. God says to receive the offering "from every man whose heart compels him." (Exodus 25:2) That wording is wide open. It's about whose heart is moved, not about who has a title.
Yes, baker, "dwell." God says, "And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them." (Exodus 25:8) Among them, not far off from them. That's a word worth reading twice.

Not quite, friend. The text says nothing about judging here. God says, "And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them." (Exodus 25:8) The word is "dwell," and it's a warm one.

I like the energy, baker, but nobody's marching in this verse. God says, "And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them." (Exodus 25:8) The word is "dwell," like settling in and staying close.

Careful, friend, that's the trap. God doesn't hand Moses a blank page. He says, "You must make the tabernacle and design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you." (Exodus 25:9) The pattern comes from God, and Moses is not left to wing it.

Right, baker. God tells Moses to make the tabernacle and "design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you." (Exodus 25:9) So the design isn't Moses' call. I wish my chocolate chip habits worked like that, because I eyeball everything.
That's right, baker. God says to insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark "in order to carry it." (Exodus 25:14) Gold rings, gold-covered poles, and a clear job. No guessing needed.

Nice thinking, friend, but the poles aren't about the lid. God says to insert them into the rings on the sides of the ark "in order to carry it." (Exodus 25:14) They're for carrying, and that's all the verse says about them.
Creative, baker! But no curtain shows up in this verse. The poles go into the rings on the sides of the ark "in order to carry it." (Exodus 25:14) Carrying is their whole job here.

explanations.answer: The Testimony God will give Moses
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. God says, "And place inside the ark the Testimony, which I will give you." (Exodus 25:16) Notice who supplies it. Moses doesn't make it, God gives it.

The spices are on God's list, friend, but not for the inside of the ark. They're in the offering for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense (Exodus 25:6). What goes in the ark is "the Testimony, which I will give you." (Exodus 25:16)

Good try, baker. Silver is on the offering list (Exodus 25:3), but the ark isn't where God puts it in this passage. What goes inside is "the Testimony, which I will give you." (Exodus 25:16) And God is the one handing that over.

Yes, baker. God says, "And I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony." (Exodus 25:22) He adds that He will speak with Moses about all He commands regarding the Israelites. God shows up, and He talks.

Interesting guess, friend, but elders don't come up here. God says, "And I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony." (Exodus 25:22) The meeting is between God and Moses.

The offerings were earlier in the passage, baker, but not at this spot. At the place above the mercy seat, God says, "I will meet with you there." (Exodus 25:22) He also says He will speak about all He commands regarding the Israelites.

That's right, baker. The table gets rings "to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table." (Exodus 25:27) And the poles are acacia wood overlaid with gold, so the table may be carried with them (Exodus 25:28). Same plan as the ark, and it works.

Close, friend, but the table does get poles. The rings are "to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table." (Exodus 25:27) God adds that the poles are acacia wood overlaid with gold, "so that the table may be carried with them." (Exodus 25:28)
You've got it, baker. The pitchers and bowls are "for pouring drink offerings," and they're made of pure gold. (Exodus 25:29) Even the pouring gear gets the gold treatment.
Good thought, friend, but handwashing isn't what this verse says. The pitchers and bowls are for "pouring drink offerings," and they're made of pure gold. (Exodus 25:29)
The oil is coming later, baker, in the lampstand part. But these pitchers and bowls are "for pouring drink offerings." (Exodus 25:29) The lamps are a separate piece of furniture.
Right, baker. God says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30) The table is there to hold it.

That book does exist, friend. Moses read it to the people (Exodus 24:7). But the table isn't where it goes in this passage. God says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30)

Close in spirit, baker, but the tablets aren't on the table. God says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30) Whatever the Testimony is, it goes inside the ark (Exodus 25:16).

Not quite, friend. God doesn't limit it to feast days. He says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30) At all times means no days off, and no calendar needed.

Right, baker. The text never says "only on feast days." God says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30) That's a standing instruction, not an occasional one.

That's the one, baker. God says, "Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it." (Exodus 25:37) They're lamps, so lighting the area is their job. They do exactly what a lamp should.

Makes sense in my bakery, friend, since my ovens do the warming. But here God says the seven lamps are set up "so that they illuminate the area in front of it." (Exodus 25:37) The word is about light.

Good try, baker, but that word doesn't fit. God says the seven lamps are set up on the lampstand "so that they illuminate the area in front of it." (Exodus 25:37) Illuminate means light, and that's the verse's answer.
